Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

          Re:      Supplement to Annual Update Regarding ISO Tariff Charges in Effect as of
                   January 1, 2026; Docket No. ER20-2054

Dear Secretary Reese:

        The Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee (“PTO AC”), on
behalf of the New England Participating Transmission Owners (“PTOs”), hereby submits to the
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the “Commission”), for informational
purposes, this letter and supporting materials that identify updated rates and associated revenue
requirements for Regional Service, Local Service and Schedule 12C Costs effective January 1,
2026 – December 31, 2026, under the Settled Formula Rate1 in Attachment F of Section II of the
ISO Tariff.2 These updated rates and revenue requirements are based on actual cost data for
calendar year 2024 and estimated cost data for calendar years 2025 and 2026. Consistent with
Section VII of the Formula Rate Protocols in Attachment F – Appendix C, this filing
(“Supplemental Informational Filing”) reflects changes to the data inputs in the annual
information filing submitted in this proceeding on July 31, 2025.3 The changes to the 2026
forecasted revenue requirement reflected in this Supplemental Informational Filing reflect
changes to the return on equity (“ROE”) pursuant to FERC Opinion No. 594, issued on
March 19, 2026.4

I.        Background of FERC Opinion No. 594

        The base ROE applicable to the PTOs is explicitly stated in Appendix A to Attachment F
of the ISO-NE OATT, which governs the calculation of each PTO’s annual transmission revenue
requirement. Appendix A currently states:

The reference to a 10.57% base ROE currently in Appendix A is the product of Commission
action in Opinion No. 531 et seq.6 Although the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
subsequently vacated Opinion No. 531 et seq. in Emera Maine v. FERC for failure to satisfy the
statutory requirements of FPA Section 206, the Commission directed the PTOs to continue
applying the 10.57% ROE on an interim basis following vacatur, rather than reinstating the
previously approved 11.14% ROE.7 As a result, the 10.57% ROE remained on file pending
completion of the Commission’s proceedings on remand and related complaint dockets.

        On March 19, 2026, the Commission issued Opinion No. 594 in the long-pending remand
proceeding arising out of Emera Maine.8 In that order, the Commission found that the
previously approved ISO-NE OATT base ROE of 11.14% was unjust and unreasonable, and
established a replacement base ROE of 9.57%, effective as of October 16, 2014.

II.         Background on the Settlement Formula Rate and Protocols under the ISO-NE
            OATT

         On December 28, 2015, in Docket No. EL16-19-000, the Commission, acting sua sponte,
established a proceeding under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act due to its concerns over
(i) the “transparency and challenge procedures with regard to the formula rates” for transmission
services by the PTOs under the ISO OATT,9 (ii) the level of “detail [used] to determine how
certain costs are derived and recovered in the formula rates,”10 and (iii) “the timing and
synchronization between the [Regional Network Service] and [Local Network Service] formula
rates.”11 A settlement resolved all issues in that proceeding12 by providing for formula rate

protocols that enhance participation by Interested Parties,13 increasing transparency in the
information the PTOs provide to Interested Parties, adopting procedures that allow Interested
Parties the opportunity to challenge the implementation of the formula rate, and reaffirming the
requirement that the PTOs make an annual filing with the Commission for informational
purposes. Many of these features are reflected in the Formula Rate Protocols (“Protocols”) that
became effective June 15, 2023, as subsequently amended.14

       Pursuant to both the Settlement and Attachment F of the ISO OATT, the PTOs are
responsible for making an annual informational filing with the Commission to reflect updated
transmission rates. Attachment F makes clear that an informational filing “does not re-open the
formula rate . . . but rather is contestable only with respect to the accuracy of the information
contained in the informational filing.”15 Section VII of the Protocols further provides that “any
changes to the data inputs … shall be incorporated into a Supplemental Informational Filing in
the same docket as the PTO’s [sic] original informational filing for the Annual Update or
incorporated as a prior period adjustment into the Formula Rate and the charges produced by the
Formula Rate in the Annual Update for the next effective Rate Year, at the discretion of the
PTO(s) … .”16

III.      Description of the Instant Supplemental Informational Filing

        The PTOs, through the PTO AC, have determined to file this Supplemental Informational
Filing in order to incorporate the replacement ROE of 9.57%, as determined in Opinion No. 594,
into the forecast component of the revenue requirements for Regional Service effective
January 1, 2026 – December 31, 2026. Updating the revenue requirements through a
Supplemental Informational Filing, rather than incorporating the ROE change through a prior
period adjustment next year, will allow ISO-NE to begin billing a lower transmission rate sooner
and then conduct rolling resettlement adjustments through its data reconciliation process dating
back to January 1, 2026, thus reflecting a resulting lower RNS rate for all billing periods in 2026.

        In accordance with Attachment F and the Settlement, a draft of the enclosed information
was posted on the ISO website for stakeholder review on June 15, 2026, and the PTOs will give
an informational presentation of the key drivers of the Regional Service (“Regional Network
Service” or “RNS”) rate changes at the Joint NEPOOL Reliability and Transmission Committee
meeting on July 16, 2026,17 and will host a Technical Session on July 22, 2026, for Interested

Parties to seek additional information and clarifications and otherwise to discuss the revenue

        The posting of the Supplemental Informational Filing on June 15, 2026, triggered the
commencement of an Information Exchange Period and a Review Period under the Protocols.18
Interested Parties have until September 15, 2026 to submit information and document requests,
and the PTOs are required to make a good faith effort to respond to all requests within fifteen
calendar days, but by no later than October 15, 2026. During the Review Period, Interested
Parties have until November 16, 2026 to submit Informal Challenges to the impacted PTOs, and
the impacted PTOs are required to make a good faith effort to respond to any Informal
Challenges no later than December 15, 2026. Interested Parties have an opportunity until
February 1, 2027 to file a Formal Challenge with the Commission.

IV.      Annual Formula Rate Updates Effective January 1, 2026

        Pursuant to Attachment F of the ISO OATT, the PTOs, except the non-FERC
jurisdictional PTOs whose ROEs were not affected by FERC Opinion No. 594,19 are submitting
herewith for informational purposes transmission rates for Regional Service, Local Service, and
Schedule 12C Costs that will be in effect for the period January 1, 2026 through December 31,
2026, that reflect changes to the return on equity (“ROE”) pursuant to FERC Opinion No. 594.

        The changes documented in this Supplemental Informational Filing result in a Pool RNS
Rate of $177.63/kW-year effective January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026. This updated
rate represents a decrease of $6.12/kW-year from the 2026 Pool RNS Rate of $183.75/kW-year
that was submitted on July 31, 2025. Attachment 1 to this filing provides the calculation of the
Pool RNS Rate effective January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026; Attachment 2 to this
filing provides the impacted PTOs’ Local Service and Schedule 12C Costs rates effective
January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026; and Attachment 3 to this filing provides the
impacted PTOs’ Annual Transmission Revenue Requirement calculations based on 2024 actual
data, and forecasted data for 2025 and 2026.
